title: How Blest Thy Creature Is, O God
description: How Blest Thy Creature Is, O God in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 44, “The happy change”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How blest thy crea-ture is, O God, When with a sin-gle eye, He views the lus-tre of thy word, The day spring from on high!

lines: How blest thy creature is, O God,
He views the lustre of thy word,
Through all the storms that veil the skies,
The Sun of righteousness he eyes,
Struck by that light, the human heart,
Sends the sweet smell of grace abroad,
The soul, a dreary province once
Feels a new empire formed within,
The glorious orb, whose golden beams,
Since first obedient to thy word,
Has cheered the nations, with the joys

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
